To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the medium spiny neuron in the striatum is selectively vulnerable in HD and that the striatum is a target of non-cell-autonomous effects.

1) striatal medium spiny neurons die in Huntington's disease, 2) striatal medium spin neurons die by apoptosis, 3) striatal medium spine neurons are selectively vulnerable to the effects of mutant huntingtin, 4) the striatum is not the sole site of mutant huntingtin-induced cell death, 5) striatal medium size spiny neurons are selectively vulnerable in Huntington's disease because they are uniquely sensitive to the effects of glutamate, 6)
the striatum, particularly the medium spiny neuron, is a key target in Huntington’s disease and that the striatal medium spiny neuron may be a key target in other neurodegenerative diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of neurodegenerative disorders, particularly Huntington’s disease.
the mechanisms of cell death in Huntington’s disease.
understanding the mechanisms of striatal degeneration in HD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the medium spiny neuron is the primary cell type that is vulnerable and that this vulnerability is both cell autonomous and non-cell-autonomous.
striatal medium size spiny neurons die in HD because of a combination of cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous mechanisms.
striatal damage is the result of a combination of cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
striatal dysfunction in HD is cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous.
HD has both cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous components and that both are necessary to understand the disease process.
striatal damage is a combination of cell autonomous and non-cell autonomous mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is considerable evidence supporting a cell-autonomous mechanism in which mutant huntingtin causes cell death in the medium spiny neuron and that there is considerable non-cell-autonomous mechanisms, in which mutant hunting tin causes cell death through cell-cell and/or region-to-region communication, in the medium spini neuron.
there is no single mechanism of HD.
there is no single mechanism that is responsible for all of the pathology in HD.
